headline: Baker Hughes deepens Hydrostor tie-up with equity investment and up to 1.4 GW of turbomachinery orders
players: Hydrostor and Baker Hughes announced a deepened strategic collaboration comprising an equity investment by Baker Hughes, amount undisclosed, and up to 1.4 GW of power generation and compression technology orders for Hydrostor's flagship projects in the United States and Australia. Baker Hughes will supply compression, expander, motor and generator technology integrated into Hydrostor's A-CAES solution. Baker Hughes has been an investor in Hydrostor since 2019 and Hydrostor described itself as nearing construction on flagship projects.
why_it_matters: Locking in up to 1.4 GW of rotating equipment with a single OEM removes the largest single supply-chain risk in A-CAES and gives lenders a bankable equipment counterparty with a balance sheet. The equity component alongside the order book means Baker Hughes is exposed to project success rather than just to a sale, which is the alignment structure that first-of-a-kind technologies typically need to reach financial close. Undisclosed investment size is the limitation; the order ceiling is a framework, not a firm commitment across all 1.4 GW. Practically this covers both Willow Rock in California and Silver City in Broken Hill, so it is a platform-level de-risking rather than a single-project item.

headline: Lightpath reports a perfect GRESB score for 2025
players: Lightpath announced it achieved a perfect GRESB score for 2025. GRESB is the ESG benchmark used by institutional infrastructure investors to assess assets and funds. No financial terms involved.
why_it_matters: GRESB scores are a procurement and fundraising input rather than a cash-flow event, but they matter at the margin for a sponsor-owned asset because European and Asian LPs use the benchmark when diligencing both individual assets and successor funds. A top score reduces friction in any future sale to an ESG-constrained buyer pool. For MSIP it is a modest supporting data point for the North Haven Infrastructure franchise. Low standalone significance.

headline: Lightpath takes third major Columbus network award, adding 55 miles for 304 route miles under construction
players: Lightpath secured its third major network award in greater Columbus, Ohio from hyperscale compute platform customers, adding 55 route miles and taking the total under construction in the region to 304 route miles, extending southwest toward Cincinnati. About 102 route miles were targeted for completion in H1 2026, ahead of schedule, with the remainder online in H1 2027. Contract value not disclosed.
why_it_matters: Three separate awards in one market from hyperscale customers is evidence of an incumbency effect: once a builder has conduit and permits in a corridor, follow-on awards go to the operator who can deliver fastest rather than cheapest. That is how a fibre platform compounds returns in an AI build-out, and it is the precursor to the Columbus-Chicago long-haul route announced in May. Delivering ahead of schedule matters commercially because hyperscale customers pay for date certainty. Watch whether Columbus route miles convert into disclosed contracted revenue and whether the Cincinnati extension attracts its own anchor.

headline: Lightpath books $252m of AI-driven contract value in 2025, up 240%, with a $6.4bn sales pipeline
players: Lightpath reported $252m of AI-enabling total contract value awarded in 2025, a 240% increase on $110m in 2024, for $362m of cumulative TCV over two years. The company reported a sales pipeline of $6.4bn, a 6.4x year-on-year increase, across 10 major operating markets. CEO Chris Morley attributed the result to execution at scale. Lightpath is jointly owned by Optimum Communications (NYSE: OPTU) and MSIP.
why_it_matters: TCV and pipeline are the forward-looking metrics that determine whether a fibre platform's capex programme is demand-led or speculative, and a 6.4x pipeline expansion is the clearest quantitative evidence that MSIP's digital asset is riding the AI infrastructure cycle rather than defending a legacy enterprise base. Contract value of this scale against a network of 12,100 route miles implies meaningful revenue per mile uplift as builds convert to service. The key caveat is conversion: pipeline is not backlog, and hyperscale demand can be redirected between markets quickly. Watch the conversion rate from the $6.4bn pipeline into signed TCV through 2026 and whether MSIP or Optimum use the momentum to test a monetisation.

headline: MIRATECH acquires Advanced Catalyst Systems of Maryville, Tennessee to expand US catalyst capacity
players: MIRATECH completed the acquisition of Advanced Catalyst Systems, a Maryville, Tennessee manufacturer of high-performance catalyst technologies and emission control systems for power generation and industrial sectors, with terms undisclosed. The combination expands catalyst production capacity across power generation, gas compression and industrial applications and integrates operations in the East Tennessee area. CEO David Zenthoefer said the deal allows MIRATECH to meet growing demand for its proprietary solutions. MIRATECH is privately held and headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma with operations across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific.
why_it_matters: Buying catalyst manufacturing rather than distribution moves MIRATECH up the value chain into the highest-margin, most supply-constrained component of emissions aftertreatment, which is the right vertical integration if engine and turbine order books are lengthening. Catalyst lead times have been a bottleneck for distributed generation projects serving data centres, so owning coating and production capacity is a competitive weapon, not just capacity addition. Combined with ECI six weeks later, this establishes a clear pattern of capability-led acquisitions across both geography and the value chain. Terms are undisclosed on both transactions, so the platform's aggregate deployed capital and sponsor identity remain unconfirmed on the public record.
